name: Achilles tendon pain (tendinopathy)
goal: Load the Achilles tendon in steady steps so it gets stronger and less painful, while you keep as active as the pain allows. Expect around 12 weeks.
whoFor: People with Achilles tendinopathy: pain and stiffness in the Achilles, worst in the morning or at the start of activity.
notFor: A sudden pop or kick-like feeling at the back of the ankle (possible rupture): get checked the same day
trackedMetric: Achilles pain on your first steps in the morning (0-10)
painRules: Pain-monitoring model: up to about 5 out of 10 during exercise is OK, as long as it settles by the next morning and isn't creeping up week to week. Running can usually continue at a level that follows the same rule.
redFlags: A sudden pop, or a feeling of being kicked at the back of the ankle
You can't rise up on your toes on that side
Calf swelling with warmth or redness (possible blood clot)
Tendon pain that started soon after a course of 'quinolone' antibiotics (e.g. ciprofloxacin): tell your doctor
Hot, red, swollen tendon, or fever

options.label: In the tendon itself, a few centimetres above the heel
Where the tendon joins the heel bone
options.hint: Insertional: avoid dropping the heel below a step or deep calf stretches.

phases.name: Settle and load gently
phases.entryCriteria: Painful tendon, especially in the morning.
phases.exitCriteria: Morning pain is easing and heel raises on both legs are comfortable.

items.note: Good for pain relief: also before a run.

phases.name: Heavy, slow strength
phases.entryCriteria: Heel raises on both legs are comfortable.
phases.exitCriteria: 20+ single-leg heel raises with little pain, and mornings are better.

items.note: Pain up to 5/10 is OK. Add a backpack when easy.
On flat ground, heels not below the toes.

phases.name: Spring and return to sport
phases.exitCriteria: Running and jumping without the tendon flaring. Keep heel raises twice a week.

references: Alfredson H, et al. 1998. Heavy-load eccentric calf muscle training for the treatment of chronic Achilles tendinosis. Am J Sports Med 26:360-6.

Silbernagel KG, et al. 2007. Continued sports activity, using a pain-monitoring model, during rehabilitation in patients with Achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled study. Am J Sports Med 35:897-906.
